physicalNotes: Radius 0.13917412 Jupiter radii from de Leon et al. 2021 (2021MNRAS.508..195D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract): 9,949.8 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00961 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: de Leon et al. 2021 (2021MNRAS.508..195D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DE_LEON_ET_AL_2021): P 3.793306 d
sources.shape: de Leon et al. 2021 (2021MNRAS.508..195D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DE_LEON_ET_AL_2021): a/R* 19.05; de Leon et al. 2021 (2021MNRAS.508..195D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DE_LEON_ET_AL_2021): inclination derived from its impact parameter 0.24 with its a/R* 19.05 (Winn 2010, eq. 7)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: de Leon et al. 2021 (2021MNRAS.508..195D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DE_LEON_ET_AL_2021): transit mid-time 2457140.22597 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 480 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
